function.mechanism: Acts as vitamin B3 source for NAD/NADP biosynthesis and energy/redox metabolism.

adi.basis: No EFSA food-additive ADI for E375 was identified from accessible OpenEFSA endpoints; E375 query returned no records.

efsa.key_finding: OpenEFSA showed niacin opinions in Nutrition and Feed Additives (latest metadata hit: 2023 feed additive output), but no directly retrievable food-additive E375 re-evaluation record.

fda.notes: Niacin is affirmed as GRAS as a direct human food ingredient for nutrient supplementation under GMP; may be used in infant formula under section 412 framework.

adi.basis: No niacin/nicotinic acid entry and no ADI were returned by queried WHO JECFA database API endpoints in this session.

concerns.summary: High-dose therapeutic niacin has shown increased adverse-event burden in modern clinical contexts without clear cardiovascular outcome benefit when added to statin-era management.
Dose-dependent adverse effects (notably flushing and hepatotoxicity risk at high prolonged doses) are consistently described for supplemental/pharmacologic niacin exposure.

no_concern_confirmed: FDA affirms niacin as GRAS for direct human food use under 21 CFR 184.1530 with GMP conditions.
No IARC monograph classification entry for niacin/nicotinic acid was identified in the checked IARC classification dataset.

adi_exceedance.notes: Typical dietary intake from foods is generally around or below low tens of mg/day in NIH NHANES summaries; exceedance concern is mainly supplement/pharmacologic exposure rather than ordinary fortification use.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory food-use status is permissive in FDA GRAS framework and no carcinogenic classification was identified; however, clear dose-related adverse effects occur at high supplemental/therapeutic doses, so classification is not risk_free.
key_factors: FDA GRAS affirmation at 21 CFR 184.1530 with GMP conditions
No direct IARC classification for niacin found
High-dose adverse effects (flushing/hepatotoxicity and broader tolerability issues) documented in reviews and clinical literature
EFSA food-additive-specific E375 ADI/re-evaluation record not retrievable in accessed endpoints
